To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the upper limit of the escape fraction of ionizing radiation that we derive from our sample of 11 z ~ 3 Lyman break galaxies is among the lowest values found so far at this redshift; (ii) this upper limit is not enough to account for the ionization rate of the intergalactic hydrogen; and (iii) the ionization rate that is required to keep the interstellar medium ionized can be accounted for by the contribution of active galactic nuclei.

the relative escape fraction of ionizing photons of L > L∗ Lyman break galaxies at z = 33 is frel esc ≤ 5% at the 1σ level, and that the hydrogen ionization rates of these sources at this redshift are not sufficient to keep the interstellar medium ionized.

the escape fraction of ionizing radiation in Lyman break galaxies at z ~ 0.3 is lower than 5%, and that the hydrogen ionization rates that we obtain are not high enough to keep the Universe ionized, unless there is a significant contribution to the UV ionization background by faint active galaxies.
